title: Fix NoMethodError when Active Job's logger is a BroadcastLogger
body:
ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger#tagged is now always defined (#58429), so ActiveJob::Logging#tag_logger could no longer rely on logger.respond_to?(:tagged) to guarantee logger.formatter responds to ActiveSupport::Logger) raised NoMethodError on
ActiveSupport::Logger::SimpleFormatter#current_tags.

Fixes [#58843](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/58843)

### Motivation / Background

<!--
Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important?
If you are fixing a specific issue, include "Fixes #ISSUE" (replace with the issue number, remove the quotes) and the issue will be linked to this PR.

This Pull Request has been created because of [this issue](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/58843).

`ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger#tagged` is now always defined (#58429), even when none of its broadcasts support tagged logging. This made Active Job wrongly assume the logger's formatter responds to `#current_tags`, raising `NoMethodError` when broadcasting to a plain, non-tagged logger.

### Detail

Before merging #58429, ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger relied on method_missing/respond_to_missing? for #tagged, so logger.respond_to?(:tagged) accurately reflected whether the underlying broadcasts supported tagged logging. That PR added a real #tagged method directly on the class, which is a behavior improvement (it now lets you use #tagged even when only some broadcasts support it) — but as a side effect, respond_to?(:tagged) became true unconditionally, for every BroadcastLogger.

ActiveJob::Logging#tag_logger uses logger.respond_to?(:tagged) as a proxy to decide whether it's safe to call logger.formatter.current_tags:

```ruby
def tag_logger(*tags, &block)
  if logger.respond_to?(:tagged)
    tags.unshift "ActiveJob" unless logger_tagged_by_active_job?
    ...
  else
    yield
  end
end

def logger_tagged_by_active_job?
  logger.formatter.current_tags.include?("ActiveJob")
end
```

With a BroadcastLogger wrapping a single plain, non-tagged logger (e.g. ActiveSupport::Logger.new(STDOUT)), respond_to?(:tagged) now returns true, so logger_tagged_by_active_job? runs — but logger.formatter there is ActiveSupport::Logger::SimpleFormatter, which has no #current_tags, raising NoMethodError.

The fix makes logger_tagged_by_active_job? check formatter.respond_to?(:current_tags) before calling it, rather than inferring formatter capability from logger.respond_to?(:tagged). A regression test performs a job with ActiveJob::Base.logger set to a BroadcastLogger over a non-tagged logger and asserts it no longer raises.
